page_intro: Monographs and major editorial projects on cultural diplomacy, East-Central Europe, and Cold War intellectual history.

items.title: A History of the Fulbright Program in Poland, 1945–2025
items.subtitle: To Build a Republic of Spirit
items.description:
This book reconstructs the history of the Fulbright Program in Poland from the postwar settlement through state socialism and the democratic transition to the present. It treats academic exchange not simply as a diplomatic program, but as a site where foreign-policy objectives, institutional ambitions, scholarly careers, and individual encounters intersected.

Its larger question is how repeated exchange helped shape Polish understandings of the United States and American understandings of Poland — and how those relationships outlived the political conditions in which they were created.

items.title: Budując Republikę Ducha
items.description: The Polish-language study from which the English Fulbright history developed.

items.title: East-Central Europe in Cold War America
items.subtitle: The Rise and Fall of an Intellectual Concept
items.description:
This book traces how “East-Central Europe” became an intellectual and political category in the United States during the Cold War. It follows scholars, émigrés, universities, journals, and Cold War institutions from interwar precedents to the late twentieth century, asking how a once peripheral regional concept became an established field of knowledge — and why its boundaries eventually moved eastward.

Key figures and institutions include Oscar Halecki, Otakar Odložilík, Piotr S. Wandycz, Columbia University, the National Committee for a Free Europe, and the institutional world that eventually coalesced around Slavic and East European studies.

items.title: Jerzy Giedroyc – Zbigniew Brzezinski. Correspondence
items.description:
A documentary edition of the correspondence between Jerzy Giedroyc and Zbigniew Brzezinski, covering more than four decades of discussion about Poland, Ukraine, Russia, the Soviet Union, and American strategy toward Eastern Europe.

The project treats their correspondence not only as a record of two prominent intellectuals, but as an entry point into the networks connecting the Paris Kultura, American Sovietology, foundations, universities, and policy circles.
